reason: E1 directly shows that annealing at 580°C for 24h introduces nano-scale L12 precipitates in the fcc phase of a related Al0.7CoCrFeNi HEA, supporting the feasibility of the intervention. E2 confirms the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic contains an L12 phase, but does not address precipitation, creep, corrosion, or thermal stability. The remaining premises on creep, corrosion, and thermal stability are not supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Annealing at ~580–600°C can introduce nanoscale L12 precipitates in the fcc phase of Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs
Such L12 precipitates are coherent and can strengthen the alloy
The AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA contains an fcc/L12 phase that can host precipitates
Nanoscale precipitates improve creep resistance by acting as dislocation obstacles
Coherent precipitates reduce corrosion initiation sites by minimizing microstructural heterogeneities
